title: Tenant-aware observability pipeline: deterministic pseudonymization, retention enforcer, and access audit
creator: Maya Gonzalez
description: Build a tenant-aware observability ingestion and downstream pipeline that removes or pseudonymizes tenant-sensitive fields deterministically, enforces retention at the dataset/tenant level, and produces cryptographic access audit trails. This ticket scopes the core pipeline and the integration points needed for tracing hooks, metric/log separation, and the dashboard-level access audit views. The goal is to allow product teams to continue troubleshooting with meaningful telemetry while ensuring PII is protected and access to raw identifiers is auditable and controllable.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic pseudonymization: sensitive fields (user_id, email, phone, session_id) are transformed using tenant-specific HMAC-SHA256 salts and reversible only with a secured KMS-wrapped key; hashes are stable across events for the same tenant.
PII-free metric exports: ingestion must split metrics from event logs and guarantee no raw identifiers are present in Prometheus/Influx exports or metric rollups.

Retention enforcer: per-tenant retention policies applied at ingestion and enforced in object storage/ES indices with automated TTL tombstoning; deletion must complete within SLA for the retention window.
RBAC and access audit: query layer records per-request access logs (who, what, why) with immutable append-only audit stream and daily signed manifests for compliance review.
Trace linkage: traces maintain non-identifying correlation keys so dashboards can show latency/error trends by anonymized cohorts without exposing PII.
Performance: end-to-end ingestion transformation latency adds <6ms p50 and <20ms p95 to existing pipeline on our standard throughput benchmark (10k events/s per shard).
False positives: automated redactors have <0.5% false-positive rate on a labeled 50k event validation set; fallback/manual unredaction workflow validated.
Canary: rollout executed to a 5% tenant canary with monitoring and automated rollback criteria defined and tested.
implementation_notes: Proposed architecture: Kafka topic ingress -> stream transformer service (KStreams/Flink) with pluginable transformers per event schema -> deterministic pseudonymizer module (tenant salt from KMS, HMAC with optional reversible encryption for support cases) -> schema registry enforcer that annotates redaction metadata -> write to two sinks: metrics pipeline (no identifiers) and logs/traces sink (pseudonymized identifiers). Store per-tenant retention metadata in central catalog and enforce TTL via lifecycle tasks that write tombstone markers consumed by storage GC. Access audit implemented as a separate Kafka topic with signed events stored to long-term WORM bucket. Use feature flags for canary and per-tenant bypass for enterprise support with audited justification.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha: enable for internal tenants only, run validation harness comparing original vs pseudonymized overlays. 2) Canary 5% external tenants for 2 weeks monitoring error/latency and false-positive redact rate. 3) Gradual ramp to 50% with expanded telemetry and dashboarding. 4) Global enable once audit trails and deletion SLA tests pass. Provide a rollback path toggling transformer to pass-through and marking affected tenants for reprocessing.
monitoring_and_metrics: Track: transform latency histogram, redact rate per-field, false-positive alerts from labeled checks, retention-enforcer success/failure rate, audit-log emission success, query latency after RBAC layer. Dashboards: PII-protection health, per-tenant retention compliance, access-audit anomalies. Alert on redact-rate spike >3x baseline or transform latency p95 >20ms.
backwards_compatibility: We will maintain original raw event writes to an internal sealed archive for 30 days (configurable per-legal hold) while outward-facing sinks only contain pseudonymized data. Support teams requiring raw identifiers must request an auditable unredaction flow which creates an entry in the access-audit topic.
